gaps: All four years used the XLT trim filter; each filtered page showed 20-31 listings, so the unfiltered fallback was not needed.
TrueCar prices are the 'Advertised price' and the page states dealer fees/add-ons are included.

page_average values come from the page's FAQ sentence 'The average price for the <year> Ford Explorer XLT is $X'. The figure is identical on the 2016, 2019 and 2024 pages ($22,923) and barely different on 2022 ($23,010), and it does not track the visible listing prices, so it appears to be a model-wide XLT average rather than a year-specific one. Compute your own mean from the listings instead.

2022 and 2024 pages skew heavily toward 4WD listings in the Northeast/Midwest; the 2016 and 2019 pages mix FWD and 4WD. The 2020+ Explorer is rear-drive based, so 2WD rows show 'RWD' rather than 'FWD'.
All four years used the XLT trim filter; each filtered page showed 29-32 listings, so the unfiltered fallback was not needed.
TrueCar prices are the 'Advertised price' and the page states dealer fees/add-ons are included.

page_average values come from the page's FAQ sentence 'The average price for the <year> Ford F-150 XLT is $X'. The figure is nearly identical across all four years ($32,770 / $32,770 / $32,901 / $32,832) and does not track the visible listing prices, so it appears to be a model-wide XLT average rather than a year-specific one. Use with caution; compute your own mean from the listings instead.
Only the first 20 of 29-32 cards per page were recorded, per the brief's cap.
The LX trim filter returned 26-30 cards on every page, so the Sport fallback was never needed; all four samples are LX-only.
First 20 of the listings on each page were recorded in page order (the pages showed 26, 30, 26 and 30 cards respectively); every recorded listing had a mileage figure.

page_average caution: TrueCar's 'average price for the <year> Honda Accord LX' text appears to be boilerplate rather than year-specific. The 2022 and 2024 pages print the identical figure ($20,412), the 2016 figure ($20,922) is well above that page's listings (which averaged roughly $14,500), and the 2024 figure is well below its listings (roughly $23,500). Use the listing rows, not page_average, for calibration.
2024 page stated two conflicting LX counts (368 and 1,634); 368 recorded. 2019 page's stated price range ($2,300 to $6,001,302) is clearly bad data on TrueCar's side.
All listings are from the first (default-sort) page, which TrueCar appears to order by its own relevance, not by price or distance; the samples are nationwide and not Charlotte-local.
2023 Touring: TrueCar stated no average for this trim

First 20 of the listings on each page were recorded in page order; every recorded listing had a mileage figure.

page_average caution: all four pages print the identical sentence 'the <year> Honda CR-V EX and <year> Honda CR-V LX averaging $24,276 and $21,621 respectively', so $24,276 is clearly a cross-year boilerplate figure, not a year-specific average. It is recorded because the page states it for that year/trim, but it should not be used for calibration; use the listing rows.
Each page also shows conflicting listing counts (e.g. '114 used 2016 Honda CR-V EX models' in the header vs '2,982' EX listings in the FAQ block); the header count is recorded.
